A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same SAeUron work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original SAeUron unlearning results in Table 1, feature-classification experiments, adversarial evaluation, and appendix experiments on generalization and activation steering.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds nudity and inappropriate-content evaluations, adversarial tests, sensitivity studies, and feature-interpretation analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 replace percentile-threshold feature selection with explicit top-τ selection and add filtering of dead and excessively frequent features. These refine feature selection while retaining the SAE architecture, training objective, negative activation scaling, and inference intervention.

E1.justification: V1 centers on UnlearnCanvas object and style unlearning. V3 adds COCO captions for training and quality evaluation, I2P nudity removal, the 143-prompt nudity attack benchmark, and broader inappropriate-content categories including hate, harassment, and violence.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the original nine comparators. New safety comparisons introduce AdvUn, Receler, MACE, CPE, SLD-M, and separate ESD-x/ESD-u variants in Table 2, plus SAFREE and RECE in Table 7. Erasediff in Table 7 corresponds to the existing EDiff comparator.

E3.justification: Object-unlearning hyperparameters change substantially between v1 Table 4 and v3 Table 5, and the reported object-classification feature budget becomes 40 features, two per class. Table 1 replaces separate domain averages with an overall average. Added protocols include SD-v1.4 nudity evaluation with a 0.6 NudeNet threshold, Q16 evaluation, 49-of-50-style unlearning, and training-size sweeps.

E4.justification: V3 adds object and nudity attack analyses, training-data/time scaling, cat–dog feature-overlap failure studies, hyperparameter sweeps, classwise retention analysis, qualitative baseline comparisons, and automated feature annotations. The original block ablation, held-out-style generalization, and activation-steering studies remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report main UnlearnCanvas results averaged over five random seeds and retain the existing uncertainty presentation in sequential-unlearning plots. No changed repeated-run protocol, confidence-interval procedure, or significance-testing practice is documented.

E6.justification: Under revised selection and tuning, Table 1 replaces object UA/IRA/CRA of 84.23/90.05/76.78% with 78.82/95.47/95.58%; these are not same-setting gains. New results include 18 nudity detections (Table 2), 1.40% post-attack nudity ASR (Table 7), and 44.6% overall inappropriate content (Table 8). Reported inference overhead also changes from approximately 10% to 1.92%.

T1.justification: Equation (5) revises the formal selected-feature set from threshold exceedance to top-τ ranking, also reflected in Appendix H. V3 corrects the input/latent dimension relationship and uses n rather than d in latent-feature summations. No new theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add an explicit claim of effective nudity removal on I2P. The abstract also softens the adversarial claim from dismissing the possibility of unwanted generation to mitigating it. The three principal contribution statements remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 adds important applicability boundaries: users with model access can remove the inference blocker, similar concepts share features, and abstract harmful concepts are poorly captured. It explains cat–dog interference through early-timestep feature overlap and interprets object-attack failures partly as classifier artifacts, supported by qualitative examples and CLIPScore analysis.

D1.justification: V3 replaces the withheld repository link with an explicit code/checkpoint link, documents the nudity experiment recipe, adds feature-preparation pseudocode, and supplies the full GPT-4o annotation prompt and sampling description. Existing SAE optimizer, hardware, and training-time details remain. However, v1's explicit DDIM sampler, guidance scale of 9, and activation-dataset size disclosures disappear.

R1.justification: V3 acknowledges concurrent Concept Steerers work, explicitly distinguishes its intervention from changing prompt embeddings or model weights, and adds citations supporting safety baselines and automated feature annotation. The central positioning around sparse-autoencoder interpretability and mechanistic unlearning remains intact; publication-year updates are largely bibliographic.

P1.justification: V3 edits the abstract and existing prose, converts several numbered subsections to paragraph headings, and reorders technical details. Pseudocode moves from Appendix I to S, while the style-classification and score-distribution appendices move from K–L to I–J. Much of the original narrative and section structure is retained.

P2.justification: V3 adds safety-result tables, feature visualizations, efficiency plots, failure analyses, sensitivity heatmaps, comparative image grids, and annotated examples. Table 1 is restructured around one overall average, the method diagram and score histogram exchange order, and the original feature-count bar chart is removed.

improvement.justification: V1's broad practical claims rely mainly on UnlearnCanvas and brief cost limitations. V3 substantially strengthens their assessment through safety benchmarks, adversarial and sensitivity studies, and interpretable failure analyses. Its explicit deployment, similarity, and abstract-concept limitations improve claim calibration. Some sampling details are lost and revised results trade lower object-unlearning accuracy for better retention, but the broader evidence and clearer boundaries provide a substantial net quality gain.
